Incident: Mimecast certificate compromise (SolarWinds/Nobelium actor)
Access path: SUNBURST backdoor in Mimecast's own SolarWinds Orion led to lateral movement into production servers; attacker stole Mimecast-issued certificates, customer server connection information and encrypted customer service-account credentials, then used a stolen certificate (authenticating Sync & Recover, Continuity Monitor and IEP to M365 EWS) to connect to customers' M365 tenants.
Orgs reached (as reported): 'Low single-digit number' of mutual customers' M365 tenants (Mimecast citing Microsoft, final report 16 Mar 2021); ~10% of customers used the affected connection (8-K, 12 Jan 2021)
Coding notes: [E048] Lateral movement and exfiltration occurred inside Mimecast; actions inside customer tenants not reported. Credentials were encrypted; no email/archive access found. 'Low single-digit' is unquantified (CEO's 'five or so' via press only). Source code downloaded without evidence of modification.
People or orgs exposed: Low single-digit number of customer M365 tenants targeted (Mimecast, 16 Mar 2021)

Incident: Click Studios Passwordstate in-place upgrade hijack (Moserpass)
Access path: Attackers compromised the upgrade director on clickstudios.com.au, pointing the In-Place Upgrade to an attacker CDN; upgrades run 20 Apr 20:33 UTC – 22 Apr 00:30 UTC 2021 downloaded a trojanised Moserware.SecretSplitter.dll whose loader fetched and ran a second stage on customer servers. Manual upgrades unaffected.
Orgs reached (as reported): No exact figure; Click Studios (Advisory 02, 25 Apr 2021): affected customers 'very low'; only in-place upgrades in the ~28-hour window; installed base ~29,000 customers (exposed, not confirmed victims)
Coding notes: [E049] Primary URLs now 404/time out; advisory facts checked via BleepingComputer quotes. Harvested system/process info, proxy credentials and password records, posted to attacker CDN daily. Execute/deploy Y because the update ran attacker code. Victim count unconfirmed.
People or orgs exposed: NR (affected customers 'very low', Click Studios, 25 Apr 2021)

Incident: CompuCom (MSP, subsidiary of The ODP Corporation) DarkSide ransomware
Access path: Attacker entered CompuCom's own IT environment (initial vector not reported), planted Cobalt Strike beacons, obtained administrative credentials and deployed DarkSide (~28 Feb–1 Mar 2021); CompuCom suspended services to and cut off access for some customers.
Orgs reached (as reported): No count. ODP filings: services to 'certain of its customers' suspended; 'impacted customers and former and current associates' later notified (10-Q Q3 2021). CompuCom: 'no indication at this time that our customers' systems were directly impacted.'
Coding notes: [E147] Cobalt Strike, admin-credential and DarkSide details only from the customer FAQ as quoted by BleepingComputer. Crossed boundary N rests on CompuCom's non-definitive statement. Data exposed / Read data rest on the Q3 2021 10-Q's mention of notices. Revenue loss $5–8M est.; $6M through Q3 2021.

Incident: Nobelium (APT29/Midnight Blizzard) campaign against cloud resellers, technology service providers and MSPs via delegated administrative privileges
Access path: Password spray, phishing, token/session-cookie theft and API abuse compromised service-provider accounts (incl. CSP Azure AD accounts with AOBO/DAP roles and a CSP VPN account); delegated admin on customer Azure subscriptions, Azure VM Run Command and authorised jump hosts used to reach downstream customer tenants; one chain crossed four providers.
Orgs reached (as reported): 140+ resellers/technology service providers notified; as many as 14 compromised since May 2021 (Microsoft, 24 Oct 2021). Downstream customers compromised via providers not counted; Mandiant reports multiple instances.

Mandiant's report (UNC3004) covers several intrusions; exfiltration, .7z archives, BEACON/CEELOADER and stopping Sysmon/Splunk are not all tied to CSP-path victims. Disable protection rests on stopped logging and monitoring.
People or orgs exposed: Up to 14 service providers compromised (Microsoft, Oct 2021); downstream customer count NR

Incident: Fujitsu ProjectWEB compromise (unauthorised access to hosted project-information-sharing tool)
Access path: Third party exploited one of several potential vulnerabilities in Fujitsu's ProjectWEB to illegitimately obtain legitimate IDs/passwords, then logged in via normal authentication appearing as an authorised user and viewed/downloaded stored customer project information (detected 6 May 2021).
Orgs reached (as reported): 142 customers in Japan (Fujitsu, 7 Mar 2022; initially 129, Fujitsu 11 Aug 2021)
Coding notes: [E225] The vulnerability is not named; the Dec 2021 notice says it was used to obtain IDs/passwords. Malware was investigated but not confirmed. Exfiltration=Y rests on Fujitsu saying data was 'downloaded'. The ~76,000 MLIT email figure and named victims (NISC, MOFA, Narita) come from news or agency statements, not checked against primary sources. ProjectWEB was shut down as remediation, not as a disruption.

Incident: Verkada support super-admin credential used to access customer cameras and Command tenants
Access path: Super Admin support credential found on an internet-exposed customer-support Jenkins server; used to log in to Verkada's Command support interface, whose session-emulation feature gave access to customers' cameras, video archives, Access Control and Wi-Fi data, and non-interactive shell commands on cameras.
Orgs reached (as reported): 97 of ~6,000 customers had video/images accessed (68 via support interface, 29 via image files on Jenkins); up to 4,530 cameras; Access Control data of 8 and Wi-Fi credentials of 8 customers; shell commands on 25 cameras in 6 orgs (Verkada report). FTC/DOJ complaint (Aug 2024): access to 150,000+ live cameras.
Coding notes: [E226] Shell commands on cameras confirmed (non-interactive reconnaissance per Verkada); root shell claimed by attackers/Bloomberg not confirmed. Verkada found no lateral movement or backdoors (N). 'Video archives' are clip saves, not T1560. Reach uses confirmed 97, not the complaint's 150,000+ cameras.
People or orgs exposed: 97 customer organisations (Verkada report v1.2, 21 May 2021); 150,000+ live cameras accessible (FTC/DOJ complaint, 30 Aug 2024)
